headline: Meet the Life Hackers
snippet: In 2000, Gloria Mark was hired as a professor at the University of California at Irvine. Until then, she was working as a researcher, living a life of comparative peace. She would spend her days in her lab, enjoying the sense of serene focus that comes from immersing yourself for hours at a time in a single project. But when her faculty job began, that all ended. Mark would arrive at her desk in the morning, full of energy and ready to tackle her to-do list -- only to suffer an endless stream of interruptions. No sooner had she started one task than a colleague would e-mail her with an urgent request; when she went to work on that, the phone would ring. At the end of the day, she had been so constantly distracted that she would have accomplished only a fraction of what she set out to do. ''Madness,'' she thought. ''I'm trying to do 30 things at once.''

headline: When Mr. Blackwell Meets Mr. Shaqwell
snippet: Commissioner David Stern said recently that he would like a new N.B.A. dress code, one requiring players to wear sportcoats, collared shirts and possibly no blue jeans at team functions and on road trips. Enforcement will not be easy, unless he enlists Shaquille O'Neal in his campaign to rid the league of players who wear sloppy, jockish or otherwise unbusinesslike attire when out of uniform and in the public eye.      Stern will do his part by fining any player who frightens small children and offends red-state sensibilities by donning a throwback jersey, blue jeans, sneakers or, God forbid, a do-rag. O'Neal, via his Mr. Shaqwell persona, can turn dress-code violators into laughingstocks with witty put-downs in the tradition of Mr. Blackwell, the Hollywood designer known for his list of the 10 worst-dressed women.
